title.narrative: Activity under preparation EU Caribbean Investment Promotion Programme (2025-2030)

description.narrative: One of the major constraints identified during the implementation of the Global Gateway Investment Agenda (GGIA) for the Caribbean is that the presence of the EU private sector in the region is lagging that of other major economic partners. In addition, EU private sector presence is not well structured around coordinating bodies such as chambers of commerce, EU Member State export agencies or other type of associations and reaching out to EU companies and investors for potential opportunities is not well systematize. Moreover, the limited scale of most of Caribbean markets, and related investment opportunities, reduces the appetite for the biggest European companies to invest in the Caribbean islands, while EU SMEs might be more interested and better fit to engage on those opportunities, but might lack the knowledge and connections to harness them.A second major constraint is that not many European Development Finance Institutions (EDFIs) are present in the Caribbean, and those that are do not usually have a region-wide scope or have operations limited to the bigger markets. For those that are present, their investment targets usually require larger ticket sizes or more advanced maturity stage of the proposal. A more flexible and swift financing format for the Caribbean private sector-led opportunities is required, in order to harness potential investment opportunities.The action will address these shortcoming and promote the Global Gateway Strategy in the Caribbean from two complementary angles: (i) establishing an investment promotion mechanism that combines coordinating and co-financing a series of investment, trade and economic missions from EU firms (SMEs) to the region, supporting the establishment of investment networks between both regions and providing market intelligence support, and; (ii) by structuring an investment promotion facility targeting the achievement of public policy objectives through EU-led, smaller-scale, private sector investments and increasing the presence of EDFIs. These components are aimed at providing horizontal support to the different GGIA projects and priorities.The programme is synchronized with other ongoing EU-supported private sector initiatives in the Caribbean, reinforcing synergies among them, as well as with the EFSD+ partners. It is aligned with the UN ¿2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development¿, specifically SDG 8 ¿Decent work and economic growth¿, SDG 12 ¿Responsible consumption and production, SDG 5 ¿Gender equality¿ and SDG 10 Reduced Inequalities, supporting mainly DAC 25010 on Business Policy and administration.
